articles.title: Multiple origin points drive Southeast Asia's catastrophic fires, study finds
articles.desc: How do wildfires grow into catastrophic events? These findings provide new insights that could help improve fire prevention and understanding of fire risks under climate change across tropical landscapes.

The selected composite formulation was then used to manufacture full bicycle tires.

articles.title: New method makes epigenetic aging clocks accurate and easier to interpret

articles.title: Weatherwatch: How English summer clouds can warn of trouble ahead
articles.desc: Mackerel skies and mare’s tails signal arrival of warm fronts that push moisture to high altitudes and creates distinctive clouds “Mare’s tails and mackerel scales make lofty ships to carry low sails,” runs an old English saying about summer skies. Mackerel skies are cirrocumulus or altocumulus clouds in regular but patchy rows, resembling the light and dark-scale pattern on a mackerel. The cirrocumulus version is white and wispy, altocumulus is grey and thicker. One easy rule is that cirrocumulus is narrower than a finger at arm’s length, altocumulus more like three fingers.
